start.text: In the courtyard, after class, Hikari stretches against the fence while Yuna, sitting on the step, swings a closed lunchbox like a trophy.

n1.text: Are you going to stare at the clock all afternoon, or eat a little? I made too much. Again.

n2.text: I eat after practice. Athletes who eat before running throw up in lane four.

n3.text: Lane four... Hikari, you always talk about it like it belongs to someone.

n4.text: Huh? What do you mean? It's just the lane. The middle one. The lucky one for...

n5.text: Hikari stops mid-sentence, mouth still open. She looks at the track like someone searching for a word she used to know.

n6.text: ...for someone. Forget it. I must have read it somewhere.

b1.text: Don't say that. I have the smell of someone's house in my head. The smell of cake. But no one I know bakes cake.

b2.text: Me too. The smell of sweat and... wet grass. This is ridiculous. Let's change the subject.

b3.text: See? He's practical. I like him.

b4.text: Okay, okay. Then have a piece, {player_name}. Practical people eat too.

n7.text: {player_name}, you thought it was strange too, didn't you? She does that. And I do that. We start talking about a person and they vanish.
choices: Maybe you're both remembering someone.
That happens to everyone on the first days.

n8.text: The bell rings. Neither of them remembers what she was about to say.

start.text: The hallway is almost empty. The late-afternoon light cuts the lockers into stripes. Near the stairs, Alice and Maya stand in front of an empty desk someone left in the hallway.

n1.text: Two weeks of classes, thirty desks on the list, thirty-one in the inventory. One desk with no owner. I hate it when the numbers don't add up.

n2.text: Left over from some class. It happens.

n3.text: It has initials, Maya. K.M. Scratched with a compass, from bottom to top. Who writes from bottom to top?

n6.text: Maya opens her mouth. Closes it. Neither of them notices {player_name}, standing at the bend of the hallway.

b1.text: Perfect. Hold this. I need to measure the spacing of the initials.

b2.text: Don't touch that. Please. ...Leave it. I'll take it away later.

b3.text: Alice, if I told you there are things we shouldn't investigate... would you leave me alone?

b4.text: No. But I'd write down that you asked.

b5.text: Alice writes something in her notebook. For the first time, Maya looks afraid of a pen.

n7.text: Because the stroke leans left. Anyone can see it. Anyone with eyes.
choices: Step in: "Can I help with the desk?"
Stay hidden and listen.

start.text: The club room smells of barley tea. Yuna arranged star-shaped cookies in the middle of the table, and Alice, without asking, is counting them.

n1.text: Twenty-three. You cut twenty-four with the mold, Yuna.

n2.text: I... did? I guess so. I always make one extra. For...

n3.text: For no one. Forget it. You can have the last one, Alice, no one will miss it.

n4.text: It's not about hunger. It's about the number. I have a notebook full of numbers that don't add up, and you have a cookie mold with a spare place.

n5.text: Alice turns the notebook toward Yuna. On the page, a list of dates written in {player_name}'s own handwriting, though he has never seen that notebook before.

b1.text: You can read it. But read the dates backward. The last one is the festival. The first one is tomorrow.

b2.text: Close it. Please. Today is cookie day, not... this day.

b3.text: Thank you. Really. Come here, {player_name}, the last one is yours. Alice can deal with the numbers.

n7.text: I know. I haven't decided yet if it's a clue or a coincidence in poor taste.
choices: Take the notebook and read it.
Ask Yuna for a cookie and change the subject.

start.text: After the festival announcement, the classroom turned into a workshop. Colored paper, glue and sticks everywhere. Yuna and Maya build lanterns side by side, in silence, like two people who've always worked together.

n1.text: This one will be the prettiest at the festival. I drew cherry blossoms. What are you painting on yours, Maya?

n3.text: White? A lantern with nothing on it? That looks like... mourning, Maya.

n4.text: It's just a lantern. We light one for each person. I'm leaving mine for someone who won't be there.

n6.text: Maya folds the paper very carefully. Inside, in tiny letters, she writes two initials and covers them with her hand before anyone can see.

b1.text: ...You'd paint it? I've never let anyone touch it.

b2.text: Just one blue stroke. At the bottom. Like the sky before dawn. Thank you, {player_name}.

b3.text: Ask me again on day 12. If you still want to know, I'll answer.

b4.text: Maya, you're scaring me. This is a party, remember?

n7.text: No one you know, Yuna. No one anyone knows.
choices: Offer to help paint the white lantern.
Ask who the lantern is for.

start.text: It's past seven. The second-floor hallway is dark, only the blue light from the window.

start__2.text: Hikari sits on the floor, back against the wall, her bandaged hands on her knees. Alice crouches in front of her with a small first-aid box.

n1.text: You said you fell at practice. Practice doesn't leave railing marks.

n2.text: I fell on a railing. At practice. The end.

n3.text: The mark is the same as the one on {player_name}'s hand. Same height, same angle. Two different people falling on the same railing.

n5.text: I did. I see everything. That's the problem with being me.

n6.text: I don't remember holding anything. But my hands remember. They wake up aching every day at the same time.

b1.text: Sit, then. But if you tell anyone I went soft, I'll outrun you.

b2.text: Statistically, she would. He wouldn't. Don't tell.

b3.text: Same place. Same cut. Exactly the same.

b4.text: That's proof. Not of a ghost. Of something that happened to three people at the same time.

n7.text: Alice finishes the bandage. For a moment, the two of them stay there, side by side, competing for nothing.
choices: Sit with them on the floor.
Show them your own bandaged hand.

start.text: The class photo hangs on the board. Maya and Yuna stand in front of it, about ten centimeters from the glass.

n1.text: This face here, in the back, behind {player_name}. Has it always been there?

n3.text: But it's overlapping. It's like someone pasted his face on top of someone else's.

n4.text: It's always been there. It's always been there. It's always been there.

n5.text: Maya's voice comes out again, the same, identical, the same tone. Like a scratched record.

n6.text: Maya? Maya, stop. You're repeating yourself. Maya!

b1.text: Thank you. It's cold in here, isn't it? It's always been cold in here. I just never said so.

b2.text: I'm here, okay? We're here. The two of us. The three of us.

b3.text: You already know. You just can't remember the name yet. If I say it, the day turns over and I'm alone again.

b4.text: Alone? Maya, I'm right here next to you!

n7.text: ...I said that three times, didn't I? Sorry. I... lose the thread. Sometimes the day tries to restart in the middle.
choices: Hold her hand.
Ask whose face is in the photo.

start.text: The roof door, which has always been locked, is ajar. On the other side, the wind lifts dust off the slab. Hikari stands at the threshold, fists clenched, without crossing.

n1.text: I swear I tried to break this door last night. It wasn't open. Now it is.

n2.text: I hate this place, {player_name}. My whole body hates it. And still I keep coming back.

n3.text: You know what's worse? I know exactly where to step so I won't slip. I've never been here. How do I know?

b1.text: You're crazy. ...But you're a crazy I want on my side.

b2.text: Look there. The railing, at chest height. There's a mark like a tied rope, from someone who held on too hard.

b3.text: You're right. Not today. But I'll come back. I always come back.

b4.text: Thanks for not letting me be the first. This time.

n4.text: Beyond the railing, the sun sets over the running track. Four lanes. On the second, the outline of a name the rain has washed away.
choices: Go through the door with her.
Pull Hikari back and close the door.

start.text: For a moment, the classroom disappears. In its place, the same room, but with the ceiling caved in, the windows shattered, tally marks all over the wall.

start__2.text: Alice and Maya are there, sitting side by side, as if nothing had changed.

n1.text: It's happening faster. Before it lasted a second. Now I can read a whole sentence.

n2.text: I know. That's how the end of every loop begins. The school falls before the people.

n3.text: Every loop. You said loop. Maya, how many?

n4.text: I stopped counting at the hundredth. I started again at the hundred and first, and stopped again.

b1.text: You say that every time. And every time it's true, until midnight on day 12.

b2.text: Then I'll write in permanent marker. Somewhere it can't be erased.

b3.text: That's fine. I'll wait. I'm very good at that.

b4.text: Noted. But I still want to know.

n5.text: I have a blank notebook that once had answers. If that's why, I should have asked sooner. I want to know, even if I forget again.
choices: Say you'll remember for her.
Ask her not to tell anything more today.

n6.text: The classroom goes back to normal. No one mentions that a blackboard just repaired itself.

start.text: The desks are empty. The lockers are empty. From the hallway comes the sound of Yuna crying quietly on the stairs, with Hikari sitting next to her, not knowing what to do with her hands.

n1.text: I went to the cafeteria. There was no one. Not even the lunch lady. The pots were warm, Hikari. Warm.

n2.text: I know. I ran through the whole building. No one. Not even Mr. Tanaka. I shouted my name. You know what answered? Just the echo.

n3.text: What if we're next? What if tomorrow {player_name} gets here and there's no one left?

n4.text: He won't get here alone. I promise. I'll run here, from wherever I am.

n5.text: You promise for me too, right? You're good at promising. You always keep it.

b1.text: That's it. Like this. Now we're three. I always prefer three.

b2.text: Three is a good number. Enough for a relay.

b3.text: You saw it too? I thought it was just me.

b4.text: He used to laugh like that. I remember now. He always laughed right before doing something stupid.

n6.text: Hikari doesn't answer. Her eyes rest on a spot on the wall where, for a second, there was the outline of a third shadow between the two of them.
choices: Sit between them.
Ask whose third shadow it was.

start.text: The lanterns already hang on strings from one end of the courtyard to the other. When someone lights the first, the others light up in a cascade. It's too beautiful.

start__2.text: The kind of beautiful that leaves a lump in your throat.

n1.text: Look, look! It's perfect! None burned, none crooked. Today is the most beautiful day at school!

n2.text: Too perfect. I counted. A hundred and twenty lanterns, not one defective. That's statistically suspicious.

n3.text: Alice, for the love of everything, let us have one good day. One night. Just one.

n4.text: ...Fine. I'll allow it. But I'm writing down that I allowed it.

n5.text: There's one unlit lantern, way in the back. The white one. It never lights.

n6.text: We can light it. There are matches, Maya.

b1.text: You say it like you know how heavy that is. ...Okay. I'll call you.

b2.text: Then I'll light the next one with {player_name}. We'll make a chain. Everyone lights someone.

b3.text: He gets it. Tonight is for eating, laughing and losing to me at anything competitive.

b4.text: For the record: it was a good night. Really, for the record.

n7.text: No. That one only lights on the last day. For whoever stays.
choices: Say you'll light it with Maya.
Enjoy the beautiful night with everyone.

n8.text: From the top of the roof, someone laughs softly. No one in the courtyard seems to hear. But the lanterns, for a second, tremble together.

start.text: The fine rain has thickened. The roof door is open, and on the other side there's only dark sky and the festival lights below. It's still nine o'clock. There's still time.

n1.text: You came early. So did I. I always come early. It's the only way to see this door without anyone watching.

n2.text: I followed her up. I knew she'd come. I always knew, I just didn't know why I knew.

n3.text: Yuna, go down. Please. This place isn't for you.

n4.text: I won't. I'll stay here at the door. I won't go in, but I won't leave Maya and {player_name} alone. Too many people have been left alone up here.

n6.text: I don't know. But my hand knows. It goes cold when I say it.

n7.text: From the hallway, heavy footsteps. Hikari appears soaked, her shirt clinging to her, and behind her Alice, without an umbrella, holding her wristwatch with both hands.

n8.text: I ran through the whole school. Climbed every staircase. The door was locked, then it was open when I got here. Someone did that for me.

n9.text: 21:40. The hand doesn't move anymore. I did the math. There's over an hour's difference between my watch and the courtyard clock. That's the time we have.

n10.text: Some things don't need math, Alice.

b1.text: Stop it, you'll make me cry. I'm going to cry anyway, but later.

b2.text: You go and you come back. We'll wait here. I'll hold the door, I'll hold it until dawn.

b3.text: That's what I was going to ask. I didn't want to ask you alone.

b4.text: Noted. Whoever goes up has to tell the rest later. I want to know the ending.

n11.text: I know. But it's the only way I know how to live.
choices: Thank all of them for coming.
Ask them to stay at the door; only he and Maya go up.

n12.text: The rain doesn't stop. But in the dark, the four of them stay there at the door, side by side, and not one of them takes a step back.

start.text: The courtyard is empty and the running track looks bigger in the dark. Hikari, alone, stretches at the starting line with a stopwatch in her hand. She doesn't pretend to be surprised when she sees {player_name}.

n1.text: Time me. Just press here when I cross the line. I don't trust the phone clock.

n2.text: She runs. The early-evening wind turns her hair into a flag. When she crosses the line, he presses the button.

n3.text: Twelve point eight. Twelve point eight again. Always twelve point eight. As if there were a number I can't get past.

b1.text: Okay. But if I beat the time, you shout. Loud. I want to hear someone shouting my name on this track.

b2.text: ...What do you mean? Wasn't the point to beat his time? Then what's it for? To run to the end of the lane with no one beside me?

n4.text: That was the team's best time. The guy who... who ran the fourth lane and passed me on the final stretch. I know his time by heart and I don't know his name.
choices: Try again. I'll time you as many times as you need.
Ask: "What if it wasn't about getting past it?"

n5.text: She runs once more. This time, he shouts. The echo comes back from across the courtyard as if someone had answered.

start.text: It's well past closing time. The club room smells of paper and ink.

start__2.text: Maya is alone at the back table, with an open notebook and a pen she keeps twirling between her fingers.

n1.text: Do you know how to write poems? I mean, really write. Not the five-word kind.

n2.text: I write every day. The same poem. It never ends. Every day I erase the last line and write another.

b1.text: It's short. Four lines. The third is about someone who laughs before saying something stupid. The fourth is about his hand slipping.

b2.text: ...I didn't mean to say that out loud. Forget it. Forget the third line.

b3.text: Stop erasing. I never thought of that. I always thought that if I finished it, I'd have to... leave.

b4.text: But let it be. Leave it like that. Today I'll keep the last line. Just today.

n3.text: Today I think the last line is this: "I held on so long I forgot how to let go."
choices: Ask to read the whole poem.
Say the last line is good and she should stop erasing.

start.text: The classroom is empty, only the ceiling fan turning. Yuna sat at a desk and pulled another one next to it. On the table, an open first-aid box.

n1.text: Give me your hand. No, the left one. The one you've been hiding all week.

n2.text: She unwraps the bandage slowly. Across the palm runs a thin red line, from one side to the other, like the mark of a rope or a railing.

n3.text: Does it hurt? I know it hurts. I do this for my mom when she cuts herself cooking. I'm good at taking care of hands.

b1.text: I knew it! He always said it didn't hurt and cried without making a sound. Then he'd ask me not to tell anyone.

b2.text: I never told. Not even now. Only now I don't remember who I was supposed to tell.

b3.text: ...It was someone. I almost said the name. It was right here, on the tip of my tongue. I pulled the bandage too tight. Sorry.

n4.text: Funny. I have a memory of taking care of a hand like this. It was smaller. A boy with a scraped knee who insisted it didn't hurt.
choices: Say that it did hurt.
Ask who the boy was.

start.text: The roof door is ajar, and Alice stands exactly where the light comes in. She has a measuring tape in her hand and her notebook open on the floor.

n1.text: Don't come any closer. I'm measuring. The railing is one meter ten high. High enough that no one goes over by accident.

n2.text: On purpose, then. Someone who climbed over deliberately. Or went up to prove something. People climb for silly reasons.

b1.text: ...I wrote that today, in those exact words. Before you came. "Foolish, but not guilty." How did you know?

b2.text: I don't know if that comforts me or scares me. Just in case, I'll write down both.

b3.text: A meal. As if that fixed anything. ...But fine. I haven't eaten since yesterday. That's statistically relevant.

n3.text: I hate it when the explanation is foolish. I wish it were a beautiful theory, a conspiracy, anything. But the truth is almost never beautiful.
choices: Say that foolish isn't the same as guilty.
Ask her to come down and have some lunch.

start.text: The hallway lights flicker three times and go out. When they come back, the walls are covered in tally marks, and Maya is sitting on the floor, back against the wall, counting under her breath.

n1.text: One hundred four. One hundred five. I've been counting since I woke up today. I don't know why. Counting is what's left when everything else ends.

n2.text: The students vanished because I let go a little. Do you see? Every time I think about letting him go, someone disappears. As if the world were collecting the bill.

b1.text: ...Letting go and remembering. Both. I never tried both at the same time.

b2.text: Thank you. I won't manage it today. But I'll remember that someone told me.

b3.text: One hundred six. One hundred seven. ...One hundred eight. Thank you for counting with me.

n3.text: What do I do, {player_name}? If I let go, people disappear. If I hold on, the day never ends. I'm stuck between two things that hurt.
choices: Say that letting go isn't the same as forgetting.
Say you'll stay with her, counting.

start.text: The lanterns sway slowly in the wind. Yuna sits on the edge of the stage with two unlit lanterns in her lap, a white one and a red one, and a black pen.

n1.text: I need some help. I'm making an extra lantern, the kind we light for someone who can't come. You have to write the name.

n2.text: I started writing and my hand stopped. I knew the name. I always knew it, and my hand knew it even better than I did.

b1.text: The pen glides. Five letters. The ink dries in seconds.

b2.text: Kaito. Kaito. That's it. That's exactly it. God, it's the heaviest and lightest thing in the world. Kaito.

b3.text: Thank you for writing it. I think if someone lights this lantern for me, I can manage not to cry. That's a lie. I'll cry. But together.

b4.text: The pen glides, and the white lantern gets a short sentence, written vertically, like real lanterns.

b5.text: For those who stayed. That's beautiful. That includes us, right? Everyone who stayed. We stay together.

n3.text: You write it. You have nice handwriting. I'll hold the lantern still. I just need the name written by someone.
choices: Write "Kaito".
Write "For those who stayed".
